                    ### Question
                    A group of scientists is conducting an experiment on the human cells involved in the immune response. They genetically modify B cells so they do not express the cluster of differentiation 21 (CD21) on their cell surfaces. The pathogenesis of which of the following organisms would most likely be affected by this genetic modification?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)
opb. Measles virus
opc. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)
opd. Human papillomavirus
ope. Parvovirus B19

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The genetic modification of B cells to lack CD21 significantly impacts the immune response to Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), as CD21 is a receptor that EBV uses to enter B cells. This results in a reduced ability to bind to EBV and an impaired immune response, aligning with the consensus that CD21 is crucial for EBV pathogenesis. In contrast, the other viruses listed (measles virus, HIV, HPV, and parvovirus B19) primarily target other cell types or mechanisms that do not directly involve CD21 on B cells. Therefore, the most affected organism by the genetic modification is EBV.
